source_text: Quod cum lucida professione inculcemus, convictus es tu publicae falsitatis, qui scribis adeo a nobis bonam defendi hominum naturam, ut sanae in infantibus negemus Christi necessariam medicinam.
pass_a_gloss: Which when we impress by a lucid profession, you have been convicted of public falsehood, who write that by us the nature of humans is so defended good that to the healthy in infants we deny the necessary medicine of Christ.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS medicina; Blaise of Christ as physician

pass_b_english: Since we repeatedly stress this in a clear profession, you are convicted of a public falsehood when you write that we defend human nature as so good that, being healthy in infants, it does not need Christ’s medicine.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Speechless newborns without rational choice; Julian's test case against inherited sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
